m_dialogEntries.m_dialog: Hmm, fascinating. This entire Citadel appears well-maintained... except this place. Why was it allowed to fall into such disrepair? What is it?
Hello Sparck. Welcome to the Virga Lab. It has been *static* days since your last visit. Security systems have been disabled. Please come inside.
This... is the Virga Lab? Interesting. Ione never spoke much of our family. This presents a unique opportunity. Shall we investigate, Wizard?
Wizard, this comms device appears to be only slightly damaged. If I can make repairs, then I can playback the last message it sent... there...
Terrible... I'm, I'm sorry. The Admiral... so much destruction. I will end this madness.
That voice... it has a ring of familiarity. Given the setting, I suspect it was my father, Keras. What was he planning with such desperation?
He was planning to betray us all. Now get out of there. The traitor's lab is forbidden.
So you're Traitor Keras' son? We thought his whole family lost in the explosion that claimed this lab. But here you are. With this... thing.
This "thing" is the Wizard. And I am growing slightly perturbed. Why do you insist on calling my father a traitor? What exactly happened here?
A lot of it is rumors, but they say Keras turned from Raven's gaze and was lost in an attempted attack on the Academy itself.
An attack? I was... unaware. If this is true, then he was, as you say, a traitor?
Yes, your father is a stain on our society. If you have the heart to hear more, talk to Praetor Drusilla in the Stronghold.
The Academy of Technologists can wait. Wizard, I must learn the full story.
Ah, Wizard. I've heard of you. The stranger who fights the Shadow with Shadow Magic. Are these rumors true?
Excellent! The Justicaria are the light that pierces the darkness, but we've had little experience against Shadow-kind. We could use practice.
Apologies, Praetor, but we were sent here to inquire about the events at the ruined lab...
And you must be Sparck. I served under your mother, herself Praetor of the Justicaria. How odd to see you here, fully grown... making demands.
Hardly a demand. Were I demanding, my voice would be 5.63 decibels louder.
Heh. How about this: if your friend goes to the Training Grounds and spars against my troops, I'll tell you everything. What do you say, Wizard?
Impossible! Can the Shadow be this strong? Or is it just you?
Looks like this little exercise was worthwhile. My troops clearly need more training. Come on back, Wizard. I'll complete my side of the bargain.
Now, Praetor, it is time you kept your word. What happened to my father? Why did your officer call him a traitor?
Because he WAS a traitor to the cause Raven gave our ancestors eons ago: prepare for the inevitable war with the Shadow.
To that end, we devote all our resources to weapons development. But some - like Keras - would rather we allocate those resources elsewhere.
And one day, your father acted on his beliefs, built a bomb to short out our weapons. A remarkably violent path to pacifism.
And the bomb went off prematurely, taking the lab with it? I see. I need a moment to parse this information. I'll await you outside, Wizard.
That boy's father cost us much, including our greatest Praetor. A traitor's son may not be himself a traitor, but there's a lot of Keras in him.
This news of my family's history is... troubling. I understand now why Ione never wished to discuss it. The memories were no doubt emotional.
I myself am not sure what to do with these revelations. There is much I must consider.
Sparck, Wizard, are you there? Looks like we're all set up over here. Get to the Royal Courtyard right away.
Yes, Captain, we are on our way. Perhaps returning to our mission will give me time to think. After you, Wizard.
You two arrived just in time.
Do forgive the stares of the crowd; we don't often get visitors. Your presence was explained to the public though, so you should be safe enough.
So tell me, where is Bat? I simply must taunt him as childishly as possible.
We are preparing him for his presentation to the public. His capture is a great victory for the Nimbari people; you'll forgive us for reveling.
Not at all. Maybe I could help. I always enjoy a good revel. Some might say too much.
As you wish. In the meantime, Sparck, you should visit the Academy of Technologists. An engineer like you might find it fascinating.
Indeed. Wizard, would you care to join me? I suspect that, with Pork by his side, Vanitus is in far less need of company.
